stories.headline: Garment unrest spreads as 264 factories shut in Savar-Ashulia
stories.summary: Garment unrest spread on 2 November as 264 factories in Savar and Ashulia declared holidays and more than 150 shut in Gazipur, a day after the wage board was formed. Ten Border Guard Bangladesh platoons and 21 executive magistrates were deployed in Gazipur, and the Dhaka-Tangail highway was blocked for hours, causing 10km tailbacks. Protesters torched police vehicles and a covered van, and police used tear gas and water cannons.
stories.why_it_matters: The unrest is now the biggest domestic story, hitting the export sector directly; the scale of closures and the security response are exam-relevant facts.
stories.exam_facts: 264 factories shut in Savar-Ashulia; more than 150 shut in Gazipur; 10 BGB platoons and 21 executive magistrates deployed in Gazipur; Dhaka-Tangail highway blocked, 10km tailbacks; police vehicles and a covered van torched; workers demand Tk 30,000 minimum wage, an end to blacklisting and reinstatement of dismissed workers.
stories.exam_relevance: High — RMG, labour unrest, law and order.
stories.key_people: Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, Superintendent, Ashulia Industrial Police-1; Amzad Hossain, Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent; Md Nurul Karim Bhuiyan, Gazipur Deputy Commissioner.
stories.figures: 264 factories shut (Savar-Ashulia); 150+ shut (Gazipur); 10 BGB platoons; 21 executive magistrates; 10km tailbacks.

stories.headline: Ministers allege masked outsiders and conspiracies behind garment unrest
stories.summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed alleged that factory owners linked to the Awami League, former MPs and former state ministers were behind the garment unrest, and said video footage showed masked men who were not workers infiltrating the protests to create disorder. The Prime Minister's adviser Mahdi Amin said evidence showed 'fugitive malign forces' infiltrating the labour movement, while senior police alleged domestic and foreign conspiracies and third-party instigation.
stories.why_it_matters: The government's framing of the unrest — sabotage rather than a wage dispute — shapes the political story and is a governance exam topic; all claims are allegations, not findings.
stories.exam_facts: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed: factory owners linked to the Awami League, former MPs and state ministers involved; masked men infiltrated protests (video footage); 24-hour surveillance and a control room at police headquarters; Mahdi Amin: 'fugitive malign forces' infiltrating; DIG Mostafizur Rahman and SP Shamima Parveen: domestic and foreign conspiracies, third-party instigation.
stories.exam_relevance: High — governance, labour politics, law and order.
stories.key_people: Salahuddin Ahmed, Home Minister; Mahdi Amin, Prime Minister's Adviser on Labour and Employment Affairs; Md Mostafizur Rahman, DIG, Dhaka Range; Shamima Parveen, SP, Dhaka.
stories.figures: 24-hour surveillance ordered; control room at police headquarters.

stories.headline: Exports rise 4.4 percent to nearly $4 billion in October
stories.summary: Bangladesh's merchandise exports rose 4.4 percent year-on-year to nearly $4 billion in October, the slowest growth since August, according to Export Promotion Bureau data. Garment exports rose 4.9 percent to $3.17 billion, with knitwear up 6.48 percent to $1.77 billion and woven garments up 2.96 percent to $1.4 billion. Exporters warned that rising costs, fuel shortages and industrial unrest could undermine growth.
stories.why_it_matters: Monthly export data is a staple of BCS/Bank economics questions, and the garment split shows which segments drive growth.
stories.exam_facts: October exports: $3.99 billion, up 4.4 percent year-on-year (slowest since August); RMG $3.17 billion (up 4.9 percent, nearly 80 percent of exports); knitwear $1.77 billion (up 6.48 percent); woven $1.4 billion (up 2.96 percent); July-October exports up 6 percent; source: Export Promotion Bureau.
stories.key_people: Asif Ibrahim, Vice Chairman, New Age Group.
stories.figures: $3.99 billion in October; up 4.4 percent; RMG $3.17 billion; knitwear $1.77 billion; woven $1.4 billion.

stories.headline: Supplementary HSC exams from 1 December as 800,000 higher-education seats may stay vacant
stories.summary: Supplementary HSC examinations for students who failed one or two subjects will begin on 1 December, with results by 31 December, the inter-education board committee said. Of 594,113 students who failed this year's HSC and equivalent exams, 422,905 failed one or two subjects. With only 646,685 of 1,240,798 candidates passing, over 800,000 higher-education seats may remain vacant, UGC data shows.
stories.why_it_matters: The supplementary exam is a new second-chance system and the vacant-seats figure shows the scale of the results crisis — both are education-policy exam material.
stories.exam_facts: Supplementary exams 1-31 December for students failing one or two subjects; 594,113 failed HSC/equivalent; 422,905 failed one or two subjects (298,040 one, 124,865 two); 646,685 passed of 1,240,798 (52.12 percent); GPA-5: 40,084 across 11 boards; higher-education seats 1.492 million, over 800,000 may stay vacant; Dhaka city pass rate 79.33 percent vs Manikganj 38.25 percent.
stories.key_people: Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, Chairman, Dhaka Education Board; ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon, Education Minister.
stories.figures: Exams 1 December, results by 31 December; 422,905 eligible for supplementary exams; 646,685 passed; 800,000+ seats may stay vacant.

stories.headline: LPG price raised by Tk 223 as 12kg cylinder now costs Tk 2,060
stories.summary: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission raised the price of a 12kg LPG cylinder by Tk 223 to Tk 2,060 for November, up Tk 475 in two months. Autogas rose to Tk 91.95 a litre from Tk 84.62. LPG has been in short supply for over a month, with consumers paying Tk 2,200-2,300 in the market against the official price, while about 10 million consumers use LPG, mostly for household cooking.
stories.why_it_matters: Fuel prices feed directly into inflation and household budgets, and BERC's monthly price-setting is a standard exam topic.
stories.exam_facts: 12kg LPG cylinder: Tk 2,060 (up Tk 223 from Tk 1,837; up Tk 475 in two months); autogas Tk 91.95 per litre (from Tk 84.62); market price Tk 2,200-2,300; about 10 million consumers; 80 percent household cooking; private sector 99 percent of the market; BERC sets prices monthly since April 2021.

stories.headline: PM orders comprehensive preparations for earthquake risks
stories.summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman directed officials to strengthen earthquake preparedness, identify vulnerable and old buildings, enforce the National Building Code and improve emergency rescue capacity. At a meeting at the Prime Minister's Office, he stressed coordinated action by ministries, local government, RAJUK and the Fire Service to protect hospitals, schools and other important establishments in Dhaka and other earthquake-prone areas.
stories.why_it_matters: Dhaka is one of the world's most earthquake-vulnerable cities, so preparedness policy is a disaster-management exam topic.
stories.exam_facts: Meeting on earthquake preparedness at the Prime Minister's Office, 2 November; directives: identify vulnerable buildings, enforce the National Building Code, enhance rescue capacity, raise public awareness; coordination among ministries, local government, RAJUK and Fire Service; attendees included Disaster Management Minister Asadul Habib Dulu and RAJUK Chairman Engr Md Reazul Islam.
stories.key_people: Tarique Rahman, Prime Minister; Asadul Habib Dulu, Disaster Management and Relief Minister; Mir Shahe Alam, State Minister for LGRD; Engr Md Reazul Islam, RAJUK Chairman.
stories.figures: Meeting held 2 November 2026 at the Prime Minister's Office.

stories.headline: Six more die of dengue as toll reaches 433
stories.summary: At least six dengue patients died and 1,970 were hospitalised in 24 hours, taking the year's death toll to 433 and cases to 138,899, the Directorate General of Health Services said. Three deaths were reported in Dhaka division, two in Mymensingh and one in Sylhet. A day earlier, eight more patients had died and 1,929 were hospitalised, with 6,114 patients under treatment across the country.
stories.why_it_matters: Dengue is Bangladesh's recurring public-health emergency; the daily toll and cumulative figures are standard general-knowledge data.
stories.exam_facts: 6 deaths and 1,970 hospitalisations in 24 hours to 8am, 2 November; total deaths 433, total cases 138,899; 6,017 patients under treatment; previous day: 8 deaths, 1,929 hospitalised, total deaths 427; source: Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

stories.headline: ACC approves three cases against Salman and son over Tk 1,121 crore
stories.summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission approved three cases against former prime minister Sheikh Hasina's adviser Salman F Rahman, his son Ahmed Shayan Fazlur Rahman and 35 others over the alleged embezzlement and laundering of Tk 1,121.49 crore from Janata Bank through fake import and export transactions. The ACC said loans were taken in the names of three companies with no prior business experience, in collusion with bank officials.

stories.headline: Sagar-Runi probe still unfinished after 131 missed deadlines
stories.summary: Investigators have failed to complete the probe into the murders of journalist Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi nearly 15 years ago despite 131 deadlines for submitting the investigation report, leaving their families waiting for justice. The task force has been given another six months, but Sagar's 74-year-old mother Saleha Monir said no one from the team had contacted her, and the High Court has summoned the ICT prosecutor and the task force head.
stories.why_it_matters: The Sagar-Runi case is Bangladesh's most famous unsolved journalist murder; the missed deadlines are a symbol of investigative failure and a governance exam topic.
stories.exam_facts: Victims: journalist Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi, murdered in February 2012; 131 deadlines missed for the investigation report (132 set); task force given another six months; High Court summoned ICT Prosecutor Tanvir Hassan Zoha and the task force head; case filed at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station by Runi's brother Nowsher Alam Roman.
stories.key_people: Saleha Monir, Sagar's mother (74); Nowsher Alam Roman, Runi's brother; Tanvir Hassan Zoha, ICT Prosecutor.
stories.figures: 131 deadlines missed; nearly 15 years since the murders; six more months granted to the task force.

stories.headline: ICT files formal charge against seven Awami League leaders
stories.summary: The prosecution submitted a formal charge to the International Crimes Tribunal against seven Awami League leaders over alleged crimes against humanity during the July 2024 uprising. The accused include former ministers Amir Hossain Amu, Abdur Razzaque, Shahjahan Khan, Dipu Moni, Mirza Azam and Faruk Khan, and former energy adviser Taufiq-e-Elahi Chowdhury. Six are in jail; Mirza Azam is absconding. The crackdown left around 1,400 protesters dead and 25,000 injured, the prosecution said.
stories.why_it_matters: The July uprising trials are the defining legal process of the post-2024 period; the charges, the accused and the casualty figures are directly askable.
stories.exam_facts: Formal charge submitted to the ICT registrar; accused: Amir Hossain Amu, Abdur Razzaque, Shahjahan Khan, Dipu Moni, Mirza Azam, Faruk Khan, Taufiq-e-Elahi Chowdhury; six in jail, Mirza Azam absconding; alleged crackdown left about 1,400 protesters dead and 25,000 injured; evidence includes the UN fact-finding report and recorded conversations.
stories.exam_relevance: High — ICT, July uprising, crimes against humanity.
stories.key_people: Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim, ICT Prosecutor.
stories.figures: Seven accused; about 1,400 dead; 25,000 injured; six in jail, one absconding.

stories.headline: Cabinet clears solar law as 4,000MW rooftop target needs $2 billion
stories.summary: The Cabinet approved the draft Special Solar Power Installation Act, 2026, to turn the Special Solar Power Ordinance into law and speed up solar installations, subject to vetting by the Legislative Division. Separately, energy specialists said Bangladesh needs about $2 billion to install 4,000MW of rooftop solar within a year, with households needing stronger incentives as the grid buys surplus power at Tk 10.50 per unit.

stories.headline: Money market rates fall in September as liquidity eases
stories.summary: Short-term borrowing costs fell in September as liquidity eased, Bangladesh Bank's Money Market Dynamics report showed. The weighted average call money rate fell to 8.48 percent at the end of September from 9.25 percent at the start, with the monthly average at 8.86 percent. The repo rate's monthly average was about 8.90 percent, and banks increasingly borrowed for seven days rather than overnight.
stories.why_it_matters: Call money and repo rates are core banking-exam concepts; the figures show how Bangladesh Bank reads liquidity.
stories.exam_facts: Call money weighted average: 8.48 percent at end-September (from 9.25 percent at the start); monthly average 8.86 percent (from 9.68 percent in July; 118 basis points lower than September 2025); repo monthly average about 8.90 percent; seven-day transactions about 50 percent of the market (from 9 percent in May); source: Bangladesh Bank Money Market Dynamics report.
stories.exam_relevance: High — banking, money market, interest rates.

stories.headline: Trump and Democrats hold final rallies before US midterm elections
stories.summary: Donald Trump and the Democrats held their final rallies before the US midterm elections, with polls suggesting Democrats are near certain to win the House and have a real chance of taking the Senate. Trump closed his campaign with a speech at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington. stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu likely to cross Andhra Pradesh coast by early 3 November
stories.summary: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu over the Bay of Bengal is likely to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, near Ongole, late on 2 November or in the early hours of 3 November, the India Meteorological Department said. stories.headline: BASIC Bank's Abdul Hye found in Canada after 'plundering' the bank
stories.summary: Former BASIC Bank chairman Sheikh Abdul Hye, accused of turning one of Bangladesh's best state-owned banks into one of its worst, has been found living in Canada with his family after leaving the country in 2023, a Prothom Alo investigation found. Loan irregularities and corruption worth Tk 45 billion took place during his chairmanship from 2009 to 2014, and the government later injected Tk 35 billion to bail the bank out. He faces at least 66 ACC cases.
stories.why_it_matters: The BASIC Bank scandal is the classic case study of banking corruption in Bangladesh; the figures and the chairman's flight are directly askable.
